name: Radha Gobind Temple
significance: A square laterite ek-ratna temple raised in 1729 by the Mallabhum king Krishna Singha Dev, its walls and cornice covered in bas-relief panels cut from individual blocks. It is a Monument of National Importance under the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Lalji Temple
significance: Built in 1658 by the Mallabhum king Bir Singha Dev, this single-towered stone temple measures about 12.3 m on each side and keeps a covered ambulatory behind three ornamented arched entrances. It is ASI-protected and part of the Bishnupur group on UNESCO's tentative list since 1998.

name: Trilok Teerth Dham
style: Modern, with Sultanate and Mughal elements
significance: A Digambara Jain temple begun under Acharya Sanmati Sagar and completed in 2015, laid out in the shape of the Jain emblem and rising 217 feet above ground with a 108-foot manastambha. Its levels model the three lokas of Jain cosmology and it houses a 31-foot image of Rishabhanatha alongside a meditation centre and dharamshala.

name: Madan Mohan Temple, Bishnupur
significance: Founded in 1694 by King Durjan Singha Dev of Mallabhum, this eka-ratna temple is faced with terracotta plaques showing Krishna-lila and the Dashavatara. It is now an ASI Monument of National Importance and no longer holds active worship.
story: Local tradition holds that during a Maratha raid the deity Madan Mohan himself fired the Dalmadal cannon, driving Bhaskar Rao's army back from Bishnupur.

name: Lakshmi Narasimha Temple, Dharmapuri
significance: A Narasimha shrine on the Godavari at Dharmapuri, raised under the Chalukyas and later enlarged by the Kakatiyas, where the deity is worshipped in seated, wrathful Ugra and peaceful Saumya forms. Subsidiary shrines include Venugopala with Rukmini and Satyabhama, and an image of Yama at the entrance.

name: Karmanghat Hanuman Temple
significance: One of Hyderabad's oldest surviving temples, dated to about 1198 CE and attributed to the Kakatiya king Prola II, where Hanuman is worshipped in a seated meditative form. The complex also holds shrines to Rama, Shiva, Saraswati, Durga, Krishna and Jagannath.
story: The king is said to have found a stone image of Hanuman while out hunting, and to have built the temple after the god appeared in his dream that night and asked for one.

name: Sitaram Bagh Temple
significance: Built in 1825 by the merchant Seth Puranmal Ganeriwala with revenue support from the fourth Nizam, this walled 25-acre Rama temple blends Mughal, Rajput and Qutb Shahi forms. Its 20-foot perimeter wall is recorded as having sheltered local people from the Razakars in the late 1940s, and INTACH lists it as a heritage building.

name: Sai Baba Temple, Dilsukhnagar
significance: Completed in 1980 and widely visited since the 1990s, this Shirdi Sai Baba shrine in Dilsukhnagar keeps Marathi prayer rituals morning and evening and draws its largest crowds on Thursdays. It was damaged in a 2002 attack and was a target during the 2013 Hyderabad blasts.

name: Gokulchand Temple
significance: Raised in 1643 by the Malla king Raghunath Singha, this laterite pancharatna temple stands 64 feet high on a 45-foot square base and is the largest stone temple in Bankura district. Its stucco decoration shows avatars of Vishnu and raslila scenes; the ASI took charge of the derelict monument in 1996.

name: Kuruvathi Basaveshwara Temple
significance: A 14th-century temple on the bank of the Tungabhadra in Hoovina Hadagali taluk, built under Vijayanagara patronage and combining Vijayanagara and Western Chalukya architectural forms. Its principal festival is Maha Shivaratri.

name: Kalachand Temple
significance: Founded in 1656 by Raghunath Singha Dev of Mallabhum, this south-facing laterite shrine is the earliest surviving eka-ratna temple at Bishnupur, about 11 m square with a corridor and three arched openings on each side. Low-relief carving covers it with Krishna-lila episodes, Puranic deities, ascetics and dancers.

name: Madan Gopal Temple
significance: Commissioned in 1665 by Churamoni Devi, queen of the Mallabhum king Bir Singha II, it is the only pancha-ratna temple at Bishnupur built in laterite. Five sikharas — an octagonal central tower with four square corner towers — sit on a curved roof above a sparsely decorated 11.3 m square plan; it is an ASI Monument of National Importance.

name: Kottankulangara Devi Temple
significance: A goddess temple at Chavara in Kollam district best known for Chamayavilakku, an annual festival in which men from across Kerala dress in women's attire and carry traditional lamps in procession to the shrine.
story: Cowherds are said to have struck a coconut against a stone near the Bhoothakulam pond and seen blood drip from it; an astrologer told them to build a temple, and because the herders had made their first offerings in women's clothing the custom endured.

name: Rajagopala Perumal Temple
significance: One of three Vishnu temples at Manimangalam near Tambaram, carrying inscriptions from 1056 CE in which Rajendra Chola I names it Kamakoti-Vinnagar and Thiruvaykulam. The settlement itself is recorded far earlier as the site of a battle between the Chalukya ruler Pulakesin II and the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I.

name: Nookambika Temple
significance: The principal goddess temple of Anakapalle, renovated in 1611 by Kakarlapudi Appalaraju Payakarao after the Golconda Nawab appointed him to govern the area. Its largest gathering falls on Kottha Amavasya, the day before Ugadi.
story: The shrine is said to have been founded for the family goddess Kakatambika, who came to be known as Nookambika, one of the nine forms of Shakti.

name: Kalarivathukkal Temple
style: Kerala, Rurujith Vidhanam with four sanctums
significance: A Bhadrakali shrine near the Valapattanam river associated with the Kolathiri rulers of Chirakkal and now a Category A temple of the Malabar Devaswom Board. The goddess is revered as the mother of Kalarippayattu, the martial art from which the temple takes its name.
story: Tradition says Annapoornashwari sailed from Kashi to Chirakkal with Kalarivatukkalamma and Madayikkavilamma to see the Krishna temple, and never went back.
